title.narrative: UNIDO: PPDP-Pathways to Profitable Dairy Farming Project
UNIDO: PPDP-Pathways to Profitable Dairy Farming Project

description.narrative:
Project key Outcomes
Goal Level: To increase incomes for smallholder farmers, particularly women and young people, in Kenya through the development of a sustainable and inclusive dairy value chain.
Purpose Level: Increased income leading to improved livelihoods and resilience among the target populations.
Outcome Level: Enhanced productivity, profitability, and inclusivity (women and youth) of the dairy sector in Kenya

The UNIDO's initiative, 'Pathways to profitable dairy farming,' is a significant step towards sustainable development in the agricultural sector. By collaborating with Tetra Pak Food for Development, this project aims to address systemic barriers that affect the participation of marginalized groups in the dairy market. Utilizing the Market System Development approach, the project will foster inclusive growth and empower the most impoverished and vulnerable communities, ensuring that they have equitable opportunities to thrive within the dairy industry.

UNIDO:s initiativ, "Vägarna till lönsam mjölkproduktion", är ett viktigt steg mot en hållbar utveckling inom jordbrukssektorn. Genom att samarbeta med Tetra Pak Food for Development syftar detta projekt till att ta adressera systemiska hinder som påverkar marginaliserade gruppers deltagande på mejerimarknaden. Genom att använda för marknadssystemutveckling kommer projektet att främja inkluderande tillväxt och stärka de mest fattiga och sårbara samhällena, vilket säkerställer att de har rättvisa möjligheter att utvecklas inom mejeriindustrin.

title.narrative: Decision on Contribution UNIDO PPDP Pathways to Profitability dairy farming project

description.narrative:
The period under review marked the inception phase, with limited concrete results expected. Key activities included the Market System Assessment (MSA), which identified feed and fodder, breeding, disease management, processing, and marketing as priority intervention areas. At the same the same time key staff were recruited to steer project implementation. At the same time, the Dairy Centre of Excellencethe core support system anchoring these interventionscommenced implementation.
Workstream 1
Capacity building of the operational team
During the reporting period, capacity strengthening of the project team continued with support from the MSD Help Desk, building on the inception phase foundations. Structured sessions deepened understanding of Market Systems Development (MSD) principles and supported the transition from analysis to implementation, with a focus on translating MSA findings into actionable interventions, strengthening facilitation skills, and advancing priority areas such as fodder systems and qualitybased milk payment systems. This ongoing support has been critical in enabling the team to operationalize interventions in a systemic and adaptive manner.
Operational Set-up
The operational setup of the project office in Githunguri was finalized during the reporting period. This included the procurement of essential furniture and IT equipment, as well as the establishment of a fully functional workspace to support daytoday project implementation and coordination with GDFCS and other local stakeholders.
Dairy Academy Development
During the reporting period, significant progress was made in advancing the Dairy Academy toward implementation readiness. Technical design work was refined through expert input, resulting in a consolidated singlephase construction approach, improved spatial layouts, and inclusivity considerations, while regulatory preparedness advanced with the completion and submission of the Environmental Impact Assessment to NEMA. Implementation planning was strengthened through the development of a detailed Gantt chart to align stakeholders on timelines and critical activities. In parallel, initial digital systems were established, including adoption of Kobo Toolbox for data collection and monitoring, ongoing work on datasharing protocols, and steps toward a shared digital repository for training materials, laying the foundation for effective operations and coordination.
Workstream 2
Strengthening extension services: recruitment, training and deployment of 19 Dairy Extension Officers (DEOs)
To strengthen extension services, 19 new Dairy Extension Officers (DEOs) were recruited, reducing the farmer-to-officer ratio from 1:700 to approximately 1:350, moving closer to the recommended benchmark of 1:200. A costing and sustainability framework was developed to guide the 15month phased employment period, and UNIDO provided a grant to support the initial deployment of the new DEOs. The deployed DEOs are strengthening lastmile service delivery through training, advisory services, and farmer outreach, while UNIDO is providing technical support on monitoring, data collection, and reporting to ensure robust performance tracking and evidencebased implementation.
Establishment of digital systems for the Dairy Academy
During the reporting period, initial steps were taken to establish digital systems to support training delivery, data management, and monitoring functions of the Dairy Academy. Kobo Toolbox was adopted as the primary platform for farmer profiling, data collection, and Monitoring and Results Measurement, alongside ongoing efforts to define secure datasharing protocols between UNIDO and GDFCS and to centralize training materials through a shared digital repository. These actions lay the foundation for an integrated digital ecosystem to support Dairy Academy operations and extension service delivery.
Capacity Building on Sustainability for GDFCS Governance
During the reporting period, the project delivered a dedicated sustainability training for the GDFCS Board of Directors to strengthen governance capacity and support the cooperatives transition toward sustainable and marketoriented operations. The training covered sustainability frameworks, supply chain and environmental management, cooperative governance, and financial literacy, and built on findings from the GDFCS sustainability assessment. Through interactive sessions, board members identified practical actions to improve milk quality, member engagement, and value creation, while integrating crosscutting considerations such as youth inclusion and inclusive governance. Overall, the training enhanced institutional capacity and ownership of sustainabilityoriented interventions, supporting the longterm viability of key project components.
Curriculum development and formalization
During the reporting period, progress was made in strengthening the content and delivery of project training. Existing training modules were reviewed and are being consolidated into a structured and accessible format for use by Dairy Extension Officers and partners. In parallel, the process of formalizing the Dairy Academy curriculum was initiated under UNIDOs technical leadership, supported by a dedicated workplan to guide standardization, consolidation, and future accreditation. These efforts aim to ensure that training delivered through both the Dairy Academy and extension services is standardized, scalable, and aligned with sector needs.
Workstream 3
During the reporting period, Workstream 3 focused on the design and structuring of interventions in the prioritized areas of feed and fodder, as well as market access and processingincluding the qualitybased milk payment system and cold chainwith technical support from the MSD Helpdesk.
Feed and fodder (incl. silage)
Workstream activities focused on designing and validating complementary feed and fodder interventions to address systemic constraints in feed availability, quality, and utilization. Three interlinked intervention tracks were developed: improved forage bundles with embedded advisory services, silage conservation kits for onfarm feed preservation, and marketbased local silage service provision models. The designs emphasize farmer adoption through demonstration farms, cooperativeled extension support, and partnerships with private input and service providers, while integrating gender and youthresponsive approaches. Progress included the development of concept notes, identification of partners, refinement of business and pricing models, and structuring of phased pilots, positioning the project for pilot rollout in the next phase in alignment with county priorities and scalability objectives.
Market access and processing (quality-based milk payment system and cold chain)
The project advanced the design and structuring of interventions to improve market access and processing efficiency, with a focus on piloting a QualityBased Milk Payment System (QBMPS) and strengthening firstmile cold chain solutions. An intervention strategy and concept note were developed with GDFCS as the anchor partner, aiming to transition from volumebased to qualitybased pricing through a phased introduction of milk quality parameters. The design was informed by a review of global best practices and partner learning, ensuring alignment with the Kenyan regulatory and sector context. In parallel, initial analysis of cold chain needs highlighted the importance of improved milk handling, cooling, testing, and traceability systems as critical enablers of QBMPS, with particular attention to inclusive adoption by women and youth.
Workstream 4
Workstream 4 focused on establishing the projects Monitoring and Results Measurement (MRM) system, with emphasis on commissioning a comprehensive baseline assessment aligned with the projects Theory of Change and Results Framework. Terms of Reference were developed to ensure robust mixed methods data collection across key outcome and impact indicators, including productivity, income, milk quality, and women and youth empowerment, and the procurement process was launched with proposals currently under evaluation. In parallel, initial steps were taken to operationalize routine MRM processes, including indicator alignment and preparation for systematic data collection through extension services and partners, laying a strong foundation for evidence based decision making and adaptive management.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
